newsitem.title: ITALY: Arbiter to assign disputed Bosnian town to Serbs.
newsitem.headline: Arbiter to assign disputed Bosnian town to Serbs.

text.p: An American arbiter has decided that the strategic Bosnian town of Brcko will be assigned to Serbs subject to international supervision and guarantees for Moslems and Croats, a senior diplomatic source said on Thursday.

The source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said arbiter Roberts Owen would announce his ruling in Rome on Friday and expected it to be supported by the multinational Contact Group on former Yugoslavia.

The dispute over the narrow Brcko land corridor, which links eastern and western halves of Serb-controlled territory in northern Bosnia, nearly caused talks on ending Bosnia's war to collapse in November 1995.

The source said Owen would announce that Brcko would be left in the hands of Bosnian Serbs, who seized the town early in the war, but would give a supervisory role to the office of Carl Bildt, the international High Representative for Bosnia.
"The handing of Brcko to the Bosnian Serbs is conditional on their good behaviour," the source said, adding that an international police presence would be arranged for the town.

The source said the Serbs would be required to allow Moslem and Croat war refugees to return to their homes and permit the Moslem-Croat Federation to use the Sava River that flows past the town as a transit trade route to the Danube.
